title: Copilot Studio: Azure SQL tables and views as an agent knowledge source
summary: The roadmap facts, Azure SQL setup instructions and consumption-based licensing are supported. The credit-control instructions omit Microsoft's warning that an environment group rule can lock the tenant-capacity setting: neither the environment UI nor the API can override it. The cited pages opened successfully; the pre-check's HTTP 429 responses did not establish missing documentation.

claims.claim: The roadmap describes Azure SQL knowledge as a way for makers to bring business data into Copilot Studio agents.
claims.quote: This enables organizations to bring business-critical information stored in Azure SQL into their agent experiences using the same knowledge-centric approach that customers already use across other supported knowledge sources.

claims.claim: The roadmap title says SQL server Support while the description refers to Azure SQL knowledge.
claims.quote: "title": "Microsoft Copilot Studio: SQL server Support in Microsoft Copilot Studio"; "description": "The Azure SQL Knowledge Source capability extends the range of enterprise data sources that makers can leverage when building agents in Copilot Studio.

claims.where: Governance guidance: Before rollout; Governance controls; rationale: risk
claims.claim: Power Platform data policies govern connector access, the class of connection used by Azure SQL knowledge.
claims.quote: Power Platform admin center data policies allow administrators to control access to these connectors in various ways to help reduce risk in your organization.

claims.claim: The general connector-blocking UI is Power Platform admin center > Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Next > connector menu > Block.
claims.quote: To add an environment to your data policy, select the environment in the **Available** tab, and then select **Add to policy**.
claims.fix: The path omits the environment and connector pickers. Use 'Security > Data and privacy > Data policy > New Policy > Next > Available > environment > Add to policy > Next > connector > ⋮ > Block' for the create-policy route; retain the general-control applicability caveat.

claims.claim: Add-ConnectorsToPolicy supports PolicyName, Connectors and Classification to classify connectors in a DLP policy.
claims.quote:
Add-ConnectorsToPolicy
    [-PolicyName] <String>
    [-Classification] <String>
    [-Connectors] <Object[]>

claims.where: controls[1].ui; Governance controls table; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: An administrator can change tenant-capacity draw for an environment through the printed Licensing > Products > Copilot Studio > Manage Copilot Credits path without an environment-group qualification.
claims.quote: If a published [environment group rule](environment-groups#rules) governs **Draw from the available capacity in my tenant**, you can't override the setting for an individual environment.
claims.fix: Keep the documented UI path, but add to controls[1].note and the corresponding governance prose: 'If a published environment group rule governs Draw from the available capacity in my tenant, the environment setting cannot be overridden. Change and republish the group rule, or remove the environment from the group before managing it independently.' Cite https://learn.microsoft.com/power-platform/admin/programmability-tutorial-manage-copilot-credit-allocations.

claims.claim: PUT licensing/allocationsV2 using version 2024-10-01 and the printed MCSMessages/TenantPool body can change environment tenant-capacity draw without an environment-group qualification.
claims.quote: Updates through the Power Platform admin center, Power Platform API, or administration SDKs are rejected with the `TenantPoolLockedByPolicy` error.
claims.fix: Retain the documented endpoint, version and body fields. Add to controls[1].note: 'If an environment group rule governs tenant-capacity draw, API updates cannot override it and fail with TenantPoolLockedByPolicy. Change and republish the group rule, or remove the environment from the group before managing this setting independently.' Use the existing API docs URL.

claims.claim: Managing Copilot Studio capacity requires Power Platform Administrator, Global Administrator or an equivalent licensing-and-capacity role.
claims.quote: Sign in as a user with the **Power Platform Administrator** or **Global Administrator** role, or an equivalent role that can manage licensing and capacity.

claims.claim: The cited Copilot Studio data-policy page requires a tenant admin or Environment Admin.
claims.quote: Be a [tenant admin](/en-us/power-platform/admin/use-service-admin-role-manage-tenant) or have the [Environment Admin](/en-us/power-platform/admin/environments-overview#environment-permissions) role.

claims.claim: The capacity controls apply across Copilot Studio workloads in the environment rather than exclusively to Azure SQL knowledge.
claims.quote: The capacity and consumption controls in the Power Platform admin center apply across Copilot Studio. They aren't exclusive to the Microsoft Copilot harness.

claims.claim: An allocation is not a spending boundary if the environment can continue drawing tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.
claims.quote: An allocation isn't a boundary if the environment can continue drawing from tenant capacity or pay-as-you-go billing.

claims.where: Governance controls; Risk assessment: Data exposure
claims.claim: The connection's database permissions and SQL network access are database-side controls rather than Copilot credit settings.
claims.quote: Credentials that can connect to the database and list and read the tables and views you plan to add.

claims.claim: Microsoft suggests testing with a diagnostic SQL view containing a small known dataset before production data.
claims.quote: Create a diagnostic view in Azure SQL that returns a small, known dataset. Confirm that the connection identity can list and read the view, then select it as a knowledge source. Test questions about that dataset before using production data.

claims.claim: Several checklist controls do not appear in the controls table.
claims.quote: Checklist: 'which makers can edit agents'; 'create a dedicated identity and views'; 'confirm the firewall or private connectivity route'. The table contains only connector data-policy classification and environment credit allocation.
claims.fix: The maker-authoring permissions, SQL identity/view permissions, SQL network configuration and agent knowledge configuration checklist steps have no corresponding table rows. With the current table retained, narrow those checklist imperatives to non-procedural considerations rather than presenting them as tabulated controls; do not add unverified rows.

claims.claim: Microsoft has not specified the precise data-policy connector classification that governs this source in the Microsoft Copilot experience.
claims.quote: Searched: site:learn.microsoft.com/microsoft-copilot-studio "Azure SQL" "knowledge" "SQL Server" "data policy". Read SQL setup, data policies, agent DLP, connector comparison and knowledge-source policy settings; no precise Microsoft Copilot SQL classification mapping found.

claims.claim: Variable cost matches the documented Copilot Credits consumption meter.
claims.quote: Usage is billed based on consumption and measured in Copilot Credits.
